# Arthropod-borne viruses

> *Viruses carried between hosts by mosquitoes or ticks, so their distribution follows the vector, which matters in Singapore.*

::: {.callout-note}
## In preparation
The plan for this chapter:
:::

| Part of the chapter | Plan |
|---|---|
| Learning objectives | Describe the group by its traits; explain one mechanism of harm for each main virus; recognise the enabling conditions that point to each |
| The group in one sentence | Viruses carried between hosts by mosquitoes or ticks, so their distribution follows the vector, which matters in Singapore. |
| Main viruses | Dengue virus; Zika virus; chikungunya virus |
| Supporting viruses | Japanese encephalitis virus |
| Later in the course | Infectious disease and public health; vector control in Singapore |
| Scenario questions | Most likely virus, with options restricted to the group; feedback names the discriminating clue |
